summary: Coconino NF lookout on Baker Butte: a 1936 CCC-built cab on a 30-foot Aermotor, earlier tower dates disputed, staffed for decades; still standing.

facts.design: 12x12 wooden live-in cab without catwalk (steel catwalk added 2008) on a 30-foot Aermotor MC-24 metal tower

staffing.status: historically staffed seasonally; no current staffing source found

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Coconino National Forest, Mogollon Rim District)

events.note: Chosen as a primary lookout with a man stationed at all times and a telephone link to the supervisor's office
H.C. Johns reported for duty as lookout man; a cabin was built for the lookout
First tower per NHLR: 6x6 wooden cab on 20-ft metal tower with ladder access. A 1922 letter describes buying a different tower, so the dates disagree
CCC replaced the first tower with the present R-3 12x12 cab on a 30-ft Aermotor MC-24; NHLR lists the build year as 1936
Forest Service officials dispute the foundation design; a June 1937 memo says the tower was not yet complete
27-mile Forest Service telephone line planned from the tower to Long Valley ranger station
Radio lookout sets planned for the Baker Butte station
Lookout usually occupied from early spring until late fall or early winter
Lookout officer snowed in during November and rescued by forest rangers
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register March 15, 2006
Steel catwalk added in the fall

evidence.supports: Mogollon Rim District; first tower was a 6x6 wooden cab on a 20-ft metal tower, constructed 1921
evidence.quote: The first fire tower at Baker Butte on the Mogollon Rim District of the Coconino National Forest was a wooden 6'x6' cab on a 20' metal tower with ladder access constructed in 1921.

evidence.supports: 1936 CCC replacement: present R-3 12x12 cab without catwalk on a 30-ft Aermotor MC-24
evidence.quote: In 1936 the CCC replaced it with the present R-3 12'x12' wooden live in cab without catwalk on a 30' Aermotor MC-24 metal tower.

evidence.supports: Administered by the U.S. Forest Service
August 1922 forest supervisor judged the purchased tower's material too light
evidence.quote: However, we are of the opinion that the material used in this tower is too light, since it was necessary to put in additional braces and struts.

evidence.supports: 1912 chosen as primary lookout, man stationed at all times, telephone link
evidence.quote: January 20, 1912: Baker's Butte was chosen as a primary lookout at which a man will be stationed at all times. The lookout has telephone connection with the Supervisor's office.
Carpenter Fisher built a cabin for the lookout.

evidence.supports: 1915 H.C. Johns reported for duty as lookout man on Bakers Butte
evidence.quote: H.C. Johns of Pittsburg, Pa., reported at the local forest office on April 18 for duty this season as a lookout man on Bakers Butte.

evidence.supports: December 1920 plan to replace the old wooden tower with a steel tower
evidence.quote: The plan was to replace the old wooden tower, which is now unsafe, before another fire season with a steel tower.

evidence.supports: August 1922 tower purchased from Baker Mfg. Co., Wisconsin; material judged too light
evidence.quote: The Baker's Butte Lookout tower was purchased from the Baker Mfg. Co., of Evansville, Wisconsin, since the price was considerably lower than that quoted by the Aermotor Company of Chicago.

evidence.supports: June 1937 memo: the tower has not been completed
evidence.quote: The Baker's Butte tower over which we seem to be arguing has not been completed

evidence.supports: 1939 telephone line planned from the tower to Long Valley ranger station
evidence.quote: Fire control will be facilitated by construction of 27 miles of Forest Service telephone line from Bakers Butte lookout tower to Long Valley ranger station.

evidence.supports: 1948 radio lookout sets planned for Baker Butte station
evidence.quote: Present plans call for lookout sets to be installed at Elden, East Pocket, and Baker Butte stations.

evidence.supports: 1953 lookout usually occupied from early spring to late fall or early winter
evidence.quote: This lookout is usually occupied more or less continuously from early spring until late fall or early winter.

evidence.supports: November 1973 lookout officer snowed in and rescued by forest rangers
evidence.quote: The Baker Butte lookout officer was snowed in completely and had to be rescued by forest rangers.
A steel catwalk was added in the fall.

evidence.supports: Rental towers are marked on the listing pages
evidence.quote: Towers that are available for rental are marked on our listing pages.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR dates the first tower to 1921; a forest letter from August 1922 describes buying a tower from a Wisconsin firm. The sources do not show whether these are the same tower, so the story gives both and does not choose one.
NHLR says the 1936 cab has no catwalk; the steel catwalk recorded in 2008 came later, so the two statements do not conflict.

notes_for_editor: No current staffing, access or rental source was found for Baker Butte, so no access level is set. The first-tower date conflicts (1921 NHLR vs 1922 letter) and the 1937 foundation dispute are both in the story. The 1912-1973 items come from West Lookouts transcriptions of Forest Service letters, not from an archive. The brief's 1936 build year matches the NHLR build field, but NHLR describes the CCC as replacing an earlier tower, so the event is recorded as replaced.
